themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 4 this week vs. a baseline of 1.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks (+191%), signaling a potential neighborhood-wide infestation that aligns with longstanding community board requests for additional building inspectors.
evidence: 4 rodent complaints this week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.65)
Spike coincides with repeated CB budget requests for additional DOB building inspectors, suggesting chronic enforcement gaps
Heat/hot water complaints (1935 over 90 days) may compound pest pressure by driving rodents indoors
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents and ask if they've noticed increased rodent activity; check with local pest control services for call volume spikes
Investigate whether DOB inspector staffing levels in CD202 are adequate; cross-reference with CB's multi-year budget requests for more inspectors

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints jumped to 3 this week vs. a baseline of 0.5 per week (+500%, z-score: 3.54), marking a fresh and unexplained shift in public safety concerns in the district.
evidence: 3 non-emergency police complaints this week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase)
Emerging signal with no prior context; requires ground-truth reporting to understand nature of complaints
Coincides with elevated noise complaints (street/sidewalk up 242% last week), suggesting possible disorder or gatherings
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD 43rd Precinct to ask what types of non-emergency calls spiked this week and in what locations
Canvass the neighborhood to identify if residents perceive a new public safety issue (disorder, gatherings, trafficking, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Noise Escalation (Street & Residential)
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints surged last week: street/sidewalk noise hit 35 complaints (+242% vs. 10.2 weekly average, z-score: 4.33) and residential noise hit 18 (+200% vs. 6.0 average), representing the sharpest sustained multi-category spike in the dataset.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 35 complaints last week vs. 10.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.33, highest severity)
Residential noise: 18 complaints last week vs. 6.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.31)
Convergence with non-emergency police spike and indoor air quality surge suggests possible event, construction, or street activity
reporting_angles: Geo-map the noise complaints to identify if they cluster around a specific block, venue, or construction site (207 DOB filings in district warrant review)
Interview residents about the nature of noise (nightlife, traffic, construction, gatherings) and timeline of onset

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 7 two weeks ago vs. a baseline of 1.4 per week (+409%, z-score: 3.01), paired with a separate outdoor air quality spike (4 complaints 3 weeks ago, +540%), suggesting systemic ventilation or pollution concerns.
evidence: Indoor air quality: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average (+409%, z-score: 3.01)
Outdoor air quality: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (+540%, z-score: 4.85, highest severity in dataset)
1935 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days suggests HVAC and building systems may be malfunctioning, compounding air quality
reporting_angles: Check NYC DEP and CEQB for any air quality advisories, industrial incidents, or pollution monitors in/near Hunts Point (a known industrial area with waste transfer stations)
Interview residents about health impacts (respiratory, asthma exacerbation); connect with local hospitals/clinics on respiratory visit trends

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints spiked to 4 two weeks ago vs. a baseline of 0.6 per week (+540%, z-score: 3.4), part of a broader pattern of water/heating system failures (1935 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days) indicating aging building infrastructure crisis.
evidence: Plumbing complaints: 4 two weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (+540%, z-score: 3.4)
Heat/hot water dominates 90-day complaints at 1935 total (21% of all complaints), with water leak (178) and paint/plaster (337) suggesting cascade failures
Aligns with CB's recurring request for additional DOB building inspectors; 166 alteration permits filed but may reflect ad-hoc repairs vs. systematic upgrades
reporting_angles: Request DOB data on violations issued for plumbing/heating code violations in CD202; cross-reference with landlord compliance history
Profile 2-3 buildings with high complaint volume (311 data can be geocoded) and investigate ownership, maintenance records, and tenant complaints
